title: Enterprise onboarding: integration, health checks, known issues, and escalation playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise customer onboarding focused on: integration guidance, health checks and QBR preparations, known issues and workarounds, and the escalation path for production incidents. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Solutions Engineers, Support engineers, and the SRE responders who will be called during escalations.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-request for enterprise customers to < 5 business days for standard integrations.
- Establish a repeatable integration checklist that can be executed by CSEs and customers.
- Define clear health check metrics and QBR artifacts so accounts are review-ready after 30/90/180 days.
- Provide a deterministic escalation path for Sev2/Sev1 issues with contact methods and runbook links.

Scope:
- Applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment customers.
- Covers initial integration, production cutover, first 90-day health checks, and escalation procedures.
- Does NOT replace product-level runbooks for model-serving runtime internals; those are linked as related pages.

Prerequisites (customer-facing):
- API key and account access configured (for Hosted / Dedicated control plane).
- Network requirements validated (eg. VPC peering, firewall rules) for Private deployments.
- Example test dataset and sample prompts for quality validation.

Roles and ownership:
1) Customer Success (owner): overall onboarding program, QBRs, escalation coordination.
2) Solutions Engineering: integration assist, SDK/CLI troubleshooting, sample code.
3) Support (owner of Tier 1 triage): ticket handling, triage, known-issues database updates.
4) SRE / Runtime team: Tier 2+ escalations for performance, availability, and kernel issues.

Onboarding runbook (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff (CSE lead):
   - Agenda: goals, success metrics, data residency, timeline, and points of contact.
   - Deliverable: signed onboarding checklist and expected milestones.
2. Credentials & Access (Day 0-1):
   - Provide API key and role-based access.
   - Verify billing and quotas for Dedicated/Hosted.
3. Networking & Security (Day 1-3):
   - For Private deployments: validate VPC config, KMS/HSM integration, and mutual TLS certificates.
   - For Dedicated: confirm IP allowlists and CIDR blocks.
4. Integration (Day 1-5):
   - Shared test app: customer clones the sample quickstart, substitutes API key, and runs an end-to-end request.
   - Verify streaming & function-call behaviors for chat workloads.
   - Validate embeddings pipeline if used (indexing + nearest-neighbor queries).
5. Load & Performance Validation (Day 3-7):
   - Run synthetic traffic: 10k requests at P95 expected latency target for chosen plan.
   - Capture token usage, batch sizes, and KV-cache hit rates.
6. Quality checks & prompt tuning (Day 3-10):
   - Run customer test prompts and record baseline quality.
   - If quality regression occurs after model swaps or quantization, raise a regression ticket tied to the prompt set.
7. Production cutover (Day 7-14):
   - Staged rollout: canary at 5-10% then 100% if health checks pass for 48h.
   - Confirm fallback policy configured (model variant / region).
8. QBR / Handoff (Day 30):
   - Deliver QBR packet: usage, latency, cost breakdown, and suggested optimizations.

Integration guide (common checks & sample commands):
- SDK quickstart (Python):
  ```python
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<API_KEY>")
  resp = client.chat.create(model="rwd-large-v2", input=[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize our product"}])
  print(resp.output_text)
  ```
- Health check curl (simple generation):
  curl -X POST 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-small-v1","input":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}' 
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat

- Recommended client-side settings:
  - Request timeout: 10s for standard low-latency routes; 30s for long-running batched jobs.
  - Retries: exponential backoff with jitter; max 3 retries for 5xx errors.
  - Idempotency keys for non-idempotent operations where possible.

Health checks & QBR artifacts (what we collect and cadence):
- Regular cadence: 30-day, 90-day, and 180-day reviews.
- QBR Packet contents (deliverable):
  - Executive summary (uptime, latency trends, cost delta).
  - Token usage and spend by route (CSV).
  - Per-model performance: P50, P95, P99 latencies, error rates.
  - Prompt set evaluation: accuracy/QA samples and regression alerts.
  - Action items: tuning tasks, caching/batching recommendations, quantization suggestions.

SLOs and thresholds (customer-facing defaults):
Metric: Uptime (control plane) | Target: 99.9% | Alert threshold: < 99.5% (30m window) | Owner: infra/SRE
Metric: P95 request latency (text gen) | Target: < 350 ms | Alert threshold: > 650 ms | Owner: runtime team
Metric: Error rate (5xx) | Target: < 0.5% | Alert threshold: > 2% | Owner: runtime team
Metric: Embeddings index latency (P95) | Target: < 200 ms | Alert threshold: > 400 ms | Owner: infra/SE

Escalation playbook (severity, criteria, and steps):
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev1 (P1): Complete production outage, blocked business functionality (major SLA breach).
  - Sev2 (P2): Degraded performance affecting multiple customers / workflows (high latency, high error rate).
  - Sev3 (P3): Minor issue with a workaround; single customer impact.

- Escalation steps (CSE / Support):
  1. Triage: gather logs, request IDs, timestamps, model/version, route, and traces.
  2. Reproduce the issue in staging or with a minimal request (if safe).
  3. Notify on-call SRE (Sev1/Sev2) or platform owner (Sev3) depending on impact.
  4. Open an incident in the incident tracker and classify severity.
  5. Communicate cadence to customer: initial update within 30 minutes for Sev1; 2 hours for Sev2.
  6. Execute runbook: link to runtime-incident-runbook and kernel-scheduling playbooks.

- Contacts (primary escalation):
  - Customer Success Pager: cs-oncall@redwood.ai (monitored 24/7)
  - SRE Pager: sre-oncall (PagerDuty)
  - Runtime Engineering (Slack): #runtime-oncall (primary responder)
  - Exec escalation (for contractual SLA breaches): csm-exec@redwood.ai

Support process & ticket lifecycle:
- Intake channels: Zendesk ticket, Support email, and in-product support button.
- First response SLA: 1 business hour for enterprise customers (during business hours), 30 minutes for Sev1.
- Triage checklist: verify account, reproduce, escalate if required, identify owner, and log mitigation steps.
- Knowledge base: update the known-issues entry after a confirmed workaround or fix.

Known issues & workarounds (short list with status):
1) Issue: Intermittent streaming stalls on long-running chat sessions (ISSUE-RT-1247)
   - Impact: Streaming response pauses after ~60s for a minority of requests.
   - Workaround: Use chunked streaming with a keepalive heartbeat (client-side), and configure shorter max_chunk_size to 4k tokens.
   - Status: In regression triage; patch deployed to canary on 2026-02-26.
2) Issue: Higher than expected latency for large embedding queries during index refresh (ISSUE-EMB-0890)
   - Impact: P95 latency spikes during index refresh windows.
   - Workaround: Schedule large index refreshes in off-peak hours; enable read-replicas for embeddings index.
   - Status: Mitigated; waiting for permanent scheduling improvement in next release.
3) Issue: 403 errors after API key rotation for some Dedicated customers (ISSUE-AUTH-0312)
   - Impact: New key not accepted by some edge proxies for 10-15 minutes.
   - Workaround: Advise customers to plan key rotation during maintenance window; clear edge cache or restart proxy if still failing.
   - Status: Root cause identified (cache TTL); fix scheduled.

Post-incident follow-up & RCA expectations:
- For Sev1: publish a postmortem within 72 hours (initial draft) and a completed RCA within 14 days.
- For Sev2: initial incident summary within 5 business days; full RCA within 30 days if customer-impacting.
- Required artifacts: timeline, impact, mitigation steps, root cause, corrective actions, and monitoring improvements.

Templates (artifacts to attach to tickets and QBRs):
- Onboarding checklist (CSV): customer, start_date, responsible, milestone_status.
- QBR slide template: one-slide executive summary, one-slide technical metrics, action-item tracker.
- Incident summary template: severity, affected customers, start/end, mitigation, owner.

Appendices and references:
- Links: runtime-architecture doc, kernel-and-scheduling playbook, enterprise-onboarding-support-playbook-2026-03-15 (related pages above).
- Internal runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-process, /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes.

Change log:
- 2025-09-15: Initial draft and distribution to CSE and SE teams.
- 2026-02-26: Added Known Issue ISSUE-RT-1247 entry and canary patch note.
- 2026-03-04: Minor edits to SLO thresholds and escalation contacts.

If you are executing this playbook and need help: open a ticket with tag #enterprise-onboarding or ping cs-oncall on Slack.
